messages:
customer_acme: Hey, getting 400 from /v1/embeddings after changing client code to batch mode. Was fine before. Curl below and response. Can someone help?

sam_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the exact request body you sent and the response headers? Also which model and request-id if present?

customer_acme: Here's the curl I sent:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"input\":\"this is a test\"}'
```
Response: 400 Bad Request
```
{\"error\":\"invalid_request\", \"message\":\"inputs must be an array of strings\"}
```
I thought single string was allowed — our client switched to sending array earlier but a refactor reverted it.

maria_devx: Yup — embeddings endpoint expects the top-level \"input\" field to be an array of strings when you want multiple items. For a single item it still needs to be `{\"input\": [\"one string\"]}`. Many JS fetch mistakes DOUBLY stringify or send raw string and end up with wrong shape.

devin_engineer: Also watch out for stringified JSON inside a string: `-d '\"[\\\"a\\\"]\"'` ends up as a single string containing brackets. That can cause dim mismatch errors downstream if a client tries to pass an array of numbers instead of array of strings. Quick repro I use:
```
# wrong
curl -d '{\"input\":\"[\\\"one\\\"]\"}' ...
# right
curl -d '{\"input\":[\"one\"]}' ...
```

sam_support: Can you check request-id in response headers or our logs? If you got retries they could look like multiple charges. We can correlate once you give a request-id or the exact timestamp window.

customer_acme: No request-id in body, header had `x-rd-request: rd_01G3...` timestamp ~1764005685. Also noticed CPU spiked and we saw a throughput drop.

ops_bot: rd_01G3... -> 1764005685 | endpoint: /v1/embeddings | status: 400 | error: \"inputs must be an array of strings\"

maria_devx: Workaround for now: wrap singleton into array in client before sending. Example JS:
```
const payload = { input: Array.isArray(items) ? items : [items] };
fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify(payload) })
```
Python:
```
payload = {\"input\": items if isinstance(items, list) else [items]}
requests.post(url, json=payload, headers={...})
```

devin_engineer: We'll add a validation patch to our SDK to coerce single strings into arrays and emit a warning. If you can share a short failing repro (paste the minimal curl or a small script) I'll add it to tests. @customer_acme willing to share?

customer_acme: Happy to share minimal repro. Thanks all :thumbsup:
